docs.title: FD-13 L1I Hit, Miss and MSHR Merge
fd13_l1i: L1I Hit, Miss and MSHR Merge
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd13_l1i is the FD-13 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. A loop inside one 64-byte line shows L1I hits; cold lines show misses and MSHR fills; and a call into the upper half of a cold line, run after a FENCE.I, makes the IFU request one line twice while its fill is outstanding, so the second request merges onto the MSHR register already fetching it. The run passes if a hit, a miss and a merge each happen at least once. DOC-007 re-timed the program: a line of filler instructions after the FENCE.I keeps the line from being fetched, and filled, before the call that should miss on it (section 2.2).

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006).

docs.title: 1.1 Files
docs.text:
DEMO=$RVA_ROOT/examples/fe_demo

File Path This file $DEMO/docs/fd13_l1i.md Program (stimulus) $DEMO/programs/fd13_l1i.svh Surfer sucl $DEMO/waves/fd13_l1i.sucl Log $DEMO/out/fd13_l1i/fd13_l1i.log Waveform $DEMO/out/fd13_l1i/fd13_l1i.fst Waveform (online) Link

docs.title: 2. Run the scenario
docs.text:
Run simulation: 

make -C examples/fe_demo fd13_l1i

View the waveform (runs simulation first if FST is not up to date): 

make -C examples/fe_demo view S=fd13_l1i

Console output: 

-I: fd13_l1i : PASS : cyc = 214

Log file output: 

-I: fd13_l1i: PASS, L1I hits 48, L1I misses 29, merges 1, events checked 8 of 8,
    cyc 214

docs.title: 2.1 What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The counts come from tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:515-526, sampled every cycle while the stream is being measured (meas).

n_l1i_hit    per bank: u_l1i.b_rsp_valid[b], summed over the 2 banks
n_l1i_miss   per bank: u_l1i.b_mis_valid[b], summed over the 2 banks
n_l1i_merge  u_l1i.u_mshr.accept && u_l1i.u_mshr.mrg_hit

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:115) is n_l1i_hit > 0 && n_l1i_miss > 0 && n_l1i_merge > 0. tb_fe_demo.sv also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors before it accepts the proof.

docs.title: 2.2 Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• Hits and misses are bank lookups, not instructions or blocks. A block needing two lines counts two lookups; a merged request counts no lookup. Wrong-path requests inside the measured window are counted too.
  • DOC-002 changed n_l1i_hit and n_l1i_miss to sum the two banks in a cycle; before, a cycle with both banks answering counted once. A DOC-002 scratch check against an independent per-bank count found no cycle with both banks answering in this run, so the figures are unchanged.
  • The merge figure is 1: the event of section 4.1, step 3.
  • Why the fillers (DOC-007). The front end runs ahead of the backend, so when the FENCE.I retires the blocks after it are already being fetched. Without the fillers the fourth call follows the FENCE.I directly: predecode finds it before the invalidate, and the block at X+0x30 requests line X at cyc 152, the cycle after the invalidate is done (l1i_ifu_inv_done at 151), so the request misses and starts a fill. The restart after the FENCE.I (a backend redirect to the next instruction, cyc 154) flushes that block; the fill goes on. The restart PC, the call, starts a block the predictors have never seen, since each block start has its own entry (BP-140), so the call is found only by predecode, once the restart's own line, invalidated by the FENCE.I, has been filled: a predecode redirect at cyc 174. X has been filled by then; the fourth call's requests for X hit, and there is no merge (L1I hits 47, misses 28, merges 0, cyc 208). With 24 fillers the call is 64 bytes past the FENCE.I. The fetch that runs past the FENCE.I before the restart still reaches it: a predecode redirect to X+0x30 at cyc 149. At cyc 154 the restart flushes the block at X+0x30. That block had not yet requested X. In the DOC-007 runs the merge needs at least 12 fillers; with 0 or 6 there is none.
  • Departure from planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md FD-13: the program adds the fillers after the FENCE.I. The proof is FD-13's.

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd13_l1i.svh, task prog_fd13. Bare M-mode, code at RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv:40); X = 0x8000_0800. Addresses are derived from the writer's emitters.

0x8000_0000  mixed(2)                                     6 bytes
top = +0x06  mixed(6)                     16 bytes, within line 0
       +0x16 bne x6,x0,top                8 passes
then four times (it = 0..3; before it = 3 a FENCE.I at +0x2C and
mixed(FD13_FILL), +0x30 to +0x6F):
             jal x1, X+0x30               call: +0x1A, +0x20, +0x26,
                                          +0x70
X+0x30       c.addi
X+0x32       jal x0, X                    back into line X
X+0x00       mixed(2)
X+0x06       jalr x0,0(ra)                return
             mixed(1)
then mixed(3), jal x0,0                   halt, at +0x7E
  • The loop of 8 passes is 20 bytes from +0x06 to +0x1A and stays in the line 0x8000_0000: after its first fill every fetch of it hits.
  • X is a cold line. The block at X+0x30 starts in the upper half of line X (offset 0x30 of 64), so it needs lines X and X+1 (IFU-7).
  • The first three calls train the predictors on the path main -> X+0x30 -> X -> main. fence_i (fe_tb_writer.svh:673) then makes every L1I line invalid; the predictors keep what they learned.
  • FD13_FILL, 24 (programs/fd13_l1i.svh), is the number of filler instructions after the FENCE.I: 64 bytes, one line. The fourth call is then at +0x70.

docs.title: 4.1 Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. Hits. L1iReadLatency is 2 (rtl/core/frontend/icache/rtl/l1i_pkg.sv:122). A hit leaves the bank's compare stage as rsp_valid = c_hit (rtl/core/frontend/icache/rtl/l1i_ctrl.sv:229, :255). In the run a request at cyc 35 (id 0, line 0x8000_0000, in the loop) is answered with id 0 at cyc 37.
  2. Misses. A miss is reported in the same stage, mis_valid = c_miss (l1i_ctrl.sv:230, :238), for the MSHR register allocated when the request was accepted; the fill comes from the memory port (l1i_mem_a_valid, l1i_mem_d_valid).
  3. The merge. On the fourth pass, after the FENCE.I, the run shows (cyc is tb.cyc, fe_tb_dut.svh:129):
  4. cyc 181: request id 0, line X (0x8000_0800), block at X+0x30
  5. cyc 182: request id 4, line X+1 (0x8000_0840), the same block
  6. cyc 183: request id 1, line X again, the predicted block at X, with u_mshr.mrg_hit set
  7. responses: id 0 at cyc 193, id 1 at 194, id 4 at 198. The IFU compares a block's first line only with the previous request's line (TD-IFU-8, rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_fetch.sv:290); the previous request was X+1, so the block at X issues its own request. The MSHR finds a valid register for line X whose data has not arrived (e_val && !e_got, rtl/core/frontend/icache/rtl/l1i_mshr.sv:232-233) and sets mrg_hit (:256, a cacheable request). A merged request does not look up the arrays (l1i_mshr.sv:309-310: b_req_valid excludes mrg_hit).

docs.title: 4.2 Reading the waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd13_l1i.sucl, which make view S=fd13_l1i opens in Surfer. Groups: clock, ftq_ifu, ifu_l1i, l1i. Look at:

  • ifu_l1i_req_val with ifu_l1i_req_paddr and ifu_l1i_req_id, and l1i_ifu_rsp_val with l1i_ifu_rsp_id two cycles later: a hit.
  • b_mis_valid, an MSHR e_val, l1i_mem_a_valid with l1i_mem_a_address, the l1i_mem_d_valid beats, e_got and b_fil_valid: a miss and its fill.
  • cyc 181 to 183: requests for X, X+1, X; mrg_hit set on the third. mrg_hit is the MSHR's match of the presented request, so it is also set in cycles with no request taken; the monitor counts it only with u_mshr.accept.

docs.title: 5. Events
docs.text: # cyc Event Other 0 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests 0x8000_0000 the same cycle fast init 1 5 first L1I miss (b_mis_valid), the cold line 0x8000_0000 2 26 first L1I hit (b_rsp_valid) 3 151 the invalidate is done (l1i_ifu_inv_done): the FENCE.I has made every line invalid 4 154 the restart after the FENCE.I: a backend redirect to 0x8000_0030, the next instruction backend 5 176 the fourth call found at F3 after the restart; predecode redirect to 0x8000_0830, X+0x30 the last 6 183 the merge: the predicted block at X requests line X while its miss is in flight (mrg_hit) the one merge 7 214 the run ends

docs.title: fe_top Connectivity Inventory
docs.text:
This file records the net-level connectivity of fe_top. The block diagrams docs/fe_block.svg and docs/fe_pipe.svg use it as the reference for connections between blocks.

Section 3 lists the nets between instances, section 4 lists the fe_top boundary ports, section 6 lists the predictors inside bp_cluster, and section 7 describes the page table walker that the testbench places beside fe_top.

docs.title: 1. Notation
docs.text:
Notation:

  • W bits is the packed width. N x W bits is an unpacked array of N elements, each W bits wide.
  • from is the instance output that drives a net, and to is the instance input that reads it.
  • bind fe_top.sv:L is the line of the port connection.
  • A file name without a directory is one of the module files listed in section 2.1.

fe_top is a purely structural module containing 7 instances, 141 nets between instances (section 3) and 75 top-level ports (section 4).

4. The fe_top boundary
docs.text:
The ports are declared at fe_top.sv:96-217 and grouped as FE-17 (planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1378) and FE-20 (planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1445) group them; fe_top.sv:29-60 restates the grouping. -> is a fe_top input read by an instance input; <- is a fe_top output driven by an instance output.

FE-17 counts two groups that cross (translation and backend) and says the instruction path is not a boundary group: what crosses is the L1I's l2-side port mem, a topology edge. FE-20 adds three inward groups (csr, config, maintenance) and one outward dependency, the ibuf read ready. The RTL carries all of them as fe_top ports; the L1I's mem port is section 4.8. Two outputs are in no group (section 4.12).

bkend_ftq_redir_val is the one fe_top net with two readers: the FTQ and the ibuf clear (fe_top.sv:44-45, IBUF-13).

docs.title: 5.2 fe_cfg member selects
docs.text: fe_cfg (fe_cfg_t, csr_pkg.sv:224-232) is not passed whole. Its members drive existing instance ports by member select (fe_top.sv:52-59, CSR-6): see section 4.10. sc_enable is the one member with two readers, the cluster and the FTQ (fe_top.sv:486, 561; FE-20 config, planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1459). fe_csr (fe_csr_t, csr_pkg.sv:236-247) is passed whole to the ITLB (fe_top.sv:788).

docs.title: 6. Inside bp_cluster
docs.text: The cluster is a four-stage pipeline (p0 to p3) with an update stage u0 and its write u1 (bp_cluster.sv:55-61). The FTQ-facing ports are grouped in the port list as follows; the predictor instances are at bp_cluster.sv:1812-2035.

docs.title: 6.1 bp_cluster port groups
docs.text:
group                                       ports at       spec
P0  prediction request, FTQ -> BPU          bp_cluster.sv:109-112
                                            ftq_bpu 3
P1  initial prediction, BPU -> FTQ          :114-123   ftq_bpu 4
RD  redirects p2, p3                        :125-131   ftq_bpu 6
SL  slot correction p2, p3                  :133-150   ftq_bpu 4a
BK  block-scalar correction p2              :152-160   ftq_bpu 4c
M2  metadata write p2 (tage ittage lp ftb)  :162-175   ftq_bpu 7.1
M3  metadata write p3 (sc)                  :177-182   ftq_bpu 7.2
UP  updates u0: ubtb lp ftb tage ittage sc  :184-224   ftq_bpu 8
RS  RAS restore, commit, flush              :226-234   ftq_bpu 8
RB  history rollback                        :236-263   ftq_bpu 9
HI  history pointer and buffer outputs      :265-271   ftq_bpu 9
CF  configuration inputs                    :273-279   FE-20 config
ST  status: init readies, queue status      :281-300   ftq_bpu 3, 8

ftq_bpu is planning/interfaces/ftq_bpu_interfaces.md.

docs.title: 6.2 Predictor instances
docs.text:
inst           module      line  stage
u_bp_history   bp_history  1815  p1 checkpoint write; history
                                 advance per predicted branch
u_ubtb         ubtb        1844  p1 (combinational from the p0 PC,
                                 registered into p1 by the cluster)
u_loop_pred    loop_pred   1861  p1, and the p2 re-read (BP-122)
u_ftb          ftb         1885  p2
u_tage         tage        1935  p2
u_ittage       ittage      1958  p2
u_sc           sc          1985  p3 (indexes at p2, answers at p3)
u_ras          ras         2013  p0 top-of-stack read, p2 push/pop,
                                 p3 repair

Stages are bp_cluster.sv:55-61 and the comments above each instance (bp_cluster.sv:1813, 1839, 1856, 1882, 1933, 1955, 1977, 2009). ubtb is instantiated with N_SLOTS = NUM_PRED_SLOTS (bp_cluster.sv:1844-1846).

  CF  ittage_enable_aging, ittage_aging_interval (1970-1971)
u_sc
  takes the TAGE p2 result (1988-1989), PC and folds staged to p2
  SL  p3 direction -> p3_slot_comb (1340), bpu_slot_val_p3 (1360)
  RD  p3 redirect -> p3_redir_comb (1289)
  M3  sc_pred_meta_p3 -> bpu_meta_sc_p3 (1791)
  UP  sc_upd_val_u0 & COND & queue room & sc_enable (1804-1807),
      sc_upd_inp_u0; arbiter sc_arb_comb (1559)
  ST  sc_ready (2005); sc_uq_not_full and sc_upd_rdy formed at
      1594-1596 from 2000-2001; sc_upd_rdy_u1 (1999)
  CF  sc_enable (2004)
u_ras
  P1  top of stack at p0 -> p1 target of a return (p1_form_comb);
      bpu_pred_ras_p1 = the p2 snapshot of the last slot (961)
  BK  bpu_blk_ras_p2 (1274)
  RD  p2 pop address -> p2_succ_comb (1107); p3 repair (1728-1730)
  RS  ras_restore_val gated by the cluster's own redirect (1402),
      ras_restore_snapshot, ras_commit_val gated by call/return type
      (1649-1653), commit br_type / ret_addr / snapshot, flush
      (2026-2034)

The p0 request reaches the table predictors only when both TAGE and ITTAGE prediction queues can accept it: w_req_val_p0 = ftq_pred_val_p0 & w_pq_rdy_p0, with w_pq_rdy_p0 = tage_pq_not_full & ittage_pq_not_full (bp_cluster.sv:634-635). The update fan-out by resolved branch type is rederived from the uBTB payload of each channel (bp_cluster.sv:1732-1746, upd_br_type at 1609-1618).

docs.title: 7. The walker beside fe_top in the testbench
docs.text:
fe_top has no walker; the testbench instantiates one beside it (FE-17 translation, planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1391; MMU-1a). The shared model rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_dut.svh holds both, included in module tb by examples/fe_demo/tb/tb_fe_demo.sv:57 and by tb_fe_top.

fe_top dut (.*)     fe_tb_dut.svh:101  every fe_top port, by name, to
                                       the tb nets of lines 27-99
ptw u_ptw (.*)      fe_tb_dut.svh:122  rtl/mmu/ptw/rtl/ptw.sv:155

What connects them, all by .* name matching:

translation group (itlb_l2tlb_interfaces.md 2)
  tb nets fe_tb_dut.svh:45-61 and 106-107
  dut.itlb_l2t_*  (fe_top.sv:143-151)  -> u_ptw ports ptw.sv:170-178
  u_ptw.l2t_itlb_* (ptw.sv:179-188)   -> dut ports fe_top.sv:152-161
walker memory port (planning/interfaces/ptw_mem_interfaces.md 3)
  tb nets fe_tb_dut.svh:108-116
  u_ptw.ptw_mem_req_* (ptw.sv:191-196) -> memory model
  memory model -> u_ptw.mem_ptw_rsp_* (ptw.sv:197-199)
  model: fe_tb_mem.svh:106-226 (initial ptw_mem at 155; ready
  pattern at 224)
walker CSR group (MMU-24a)
  ptw_csr  fe_tb_dut.svh:117 -> u_ptw.ptw_csr ptw.sv:206
  driven by csr_sync, fe_tb_csr.svh:29 (csr_tb_pkg::pack_ptw_csr)
the L1I mem link (section 4.8)
  answered by the same memory model, fe_tb_mem.svh:35-103
  (a_ready at 35, the D-channel responder initial tl_mem at 37)

The walker and the L1I read one memory image (fe_tb_mem.svh; FE-21, planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1490, ptw_mem_interfaces.md WM-10, line 143). fe_csr and ptw_csr are packed from the one csr_tb_pkg shadow (fe_tb_dut.svh:119-121).

docs.title: 8. Disagreements between the RTL and the planning documents
docs.text:
The RTL is what sections 2 to 7 record.

D1  FTB update port count.
    RTL: 15 payload ports plus the valid (fe_top.sv:274-289;
    bp_cluster.sv:195-211). The comments fe_top.sv:69, fe_top.sv:273,
    bp_cluster.sv:194 and ftq.sv:200 say 14.
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8 says 15 (lines 883, 895-900; "This
    read 14"). The plan agrees with the ports; the four RTL comments
    are stale since BP-121 added ftb_upd_jmp_rvc_u0.

D2  ITTAGE update payload name.
    RTL: ittage_upd_inp_u0 (fe_top.sv:298; bp_cluster.sv:219-220;
    ftq port bound at fe_top.sv:568).
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8 table, line 885, "ittage_upd_inp".

D3  TAGE and ITTAGE queue status port names (TD#49).
    RTL: tage.sv:47-48 and ittage.sv:46-47 declare <p>_pq_not_full and
    <p>_uq_not_full; bp_cluster.sv:1945-1946 and 1968-1969 bind them;
    bp_cluster.sv:286-288 says TD#49 was applied by BP-132.
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8, lines 947-956, says tage and
    ittage declare pq_not_full and upd_rdy without prefix and that
    TD#49 is not yet applied. The cluster boundary names (tage_upd_rdy,
    ittage_upd_rdy) agree with lines 938-939.

D4  uBTB update port at the cluster boundary.
    RTL: ubtb_upd_u0, ubtb_upd_t [NUM_PRED_SLOTS-1:0], 352 bits
    (bp_cluster.sv:186; fe_top.sv:292).
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8 (line 881) names only the predictor
    port upd_u0; no planning document names the boundary port.

D5  Observation outputs.
    RTL: ftq_full and ftq_empty are fe_top outputs (fe_top.sv:212-216).
    Plan: in no FE-17 or FE-20 group (fe_decisions.md:1378, 1445) and
    named by no interface document.

D6  Decode outputs.
    RTL: decode_bundle, vec_decode_bundle, is_vector, pd_out,
    vtype_hazard (fe_top.sv:103-107), from u_dec (fe_top.sv:820-824).
    Plan: FE-17 backend (fe_decisions.md:1410) says "decode to rename
    and dispatch" with no port list; no interface document names
    decode_bundle, vec_decode_bundle or pd_out (is_vector and
    vtype_hazard appear in dcd_decisions.md:612 and 262).

D7  The instruction group.
    RTL: fe_top.sv:30-32 lists "instruction" as a boundary group, the
    20 l1i_mem_* ports (fe_top.sv:167-186).
    Plan: FE-17 (fe_decisions.md:1378, 1385) counts two groups and
    says the instruction path is not a boundary group, its `mem` port
    being a topology edge; FE-21 (fe_decisions.md:1479, 1490) says the
    port leaves the top as a boundary edge. The ports are the same;
    the documents count them differently.

D8  The config group comment.
    RTL: fe_top.sv:52-54 says "see Results Capture for the ones FE-20
    does not list".
    Plan: FE-20 config (fe_decisions.md:1459-1468) now lists every
    member fe_top distributes (sc_enable, ftb_fastpath_en, the four
    aging inputs, ext_enable); the comment refers to the text before
    the BP-118 correction.

D9  Walker-side labels.
    RTL: the server of the translation group is the page table walker
    (fe_tb_dut.svh:122; fe_top.sv:33-36).
    Plan: itlb_l2tlb_interfaces.md 2 (lines 44-63) labels the far end
    "L2TLB" while its line 22 says the server is the walker. Naming
    only; ports and widths agree.

No width disagreement was found: every port width in ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 3 and 8, ftq_ifu_interfaces.md 4 to 6, l1i_ifu_interfaces.md 4.1, 5.1, 10.1 and 11.2, itlb_ifu_interfaces.md 2, ifu_ibuf_interfaces.md 2, ftq_backend_interfaces.md 4 to 6, itlb_l2tlb_interfaces.md 2 and ptw_mem_interfaces.md 3 that was compared resolves to the elaborated width recorded here.
